message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)**  

| Topic | What You Need to Know | Practical Tips |
|-------|----------------------|----------------|
| **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law. • 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on city streets. • “No speed limit” roads allow up to 75 mph if posted. | • Always obey posted signs; use a GPS that updates speed limits. |
| **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts. • Children under 8 must be in a child‑seat or booster. | • Check the seat‑belt sign on the rear window; it’s a reminder for all passengers. |
| **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is illegal while driving. • Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Install a Bluetooth or voice‑activated system before you drive. |
| **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal. • Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | • Designate a sober driver or use rideshare if you’ve had a drink. |
| **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green = go; yellow = prepare to stop. • Stop signs require a full stop. | • Use a “stop‑and‑look” approach at intersections. |
| **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority. • Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks. | • Yield to pedestrians and cyclists. |
| **Lane Discipline** | • Keep left unless passing or turning right. • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | • Check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. |
| **School Bus** | • Stop 20 ft from a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop sign extended. | • Do not pass a stopped school bus until the lights are off. |
| **Toll Roads** | • Texas has electronic toll collection (TxTag). • Manual tolls are collected at booths. | • Keep your TxTag account funded or use a toll‑by‑mail option. |
| **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, on sidewalks, or in no‑parking zones. • Pay attention to meter times and parking signs. | • Use parking apps to avoid tickets. |
| **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display a valid registration sticker. • Minimum liability insurance is required. | • Keep proof of insurance in the glove compartment. |
| **Driving Under the Influence of Drugs** | • Prescription drugs that impair driving are treated like alcohol. | • If you’re unsure, err on the side of caution and avoid driving. |
| **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles must wear helmets. • Commercial vehicles must follow specific weight and size limits. | • Check the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) for commercial regulations. |

### Quick Resources

| Resource | What It Offers | How to Access |
|----------|----------------|---------------|
| **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** | Driver’s license info, traffic laws, and safety tips | https://www.dps.texas.gov |
| **TxDOT Traffic Laws** | Detailed statutes and regulations | https://www.txdot.gov |
| **Texas Highway Patrol** | Enforcement news, safety campaigns | https://www.txdps.gov/HighwayPatrol |
| **Texas Toll Road Authority** | Toll rates, TxTag info | https://www.ttra.com |
| **Texas Insurance Commission** | Insurance requirements | https://www.tic.texas.gov |

---

#### Quick FAQ

1. **Can I use my phone while driving?**  
   Only hands‑free. Hand‑held use is illegal.

2. **What if I’m pulled over for a broken taillight?**  
   You’ll likely receive a ticket; fix it promptly to avoid further penalties.

3. **Do I need a special license to drive a motorcycle?**  
   Yes, a motorcycle endorsement (Class M) is required.

4. **What happens if I get a DUI?**  
   Penalties include fines, license suspension, possible jail time, and mandatory alcohol education programs.

5. **Is it okay to drive through a red light if no one is there?**  
   No. Red lights are mandatory stops regardless of traffic presence.

Feel free to ask if you need deeper details on any specific law or scenario!
